title: regional-failover-circuit-breaker-with-priority-degradation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a regional circuit breaker that triggers prioritized degradation routes instead of full traffic tear-down; includes observability and safe rollback. Improves resiliency during partial region outages and reduces cross-region blast radius.
description: Context: During a recent partial-region networking incident we observed aggressive global reroutes causing cache thrash and downstream tail latency spikes. This PR introduces a regional circuit breaker that transitions traffic for affected origin regions into prioritized degradation plans (tiered fallbacks, reduced batch sizes, and permissive KV-cache reads) instead of immediate full failover. Motivation: minimize user-visible errors while preserving SLOs for unaffected regions and limit cross-region capacity pressure. Summary of changes: 1) runtime: add RegionalCircuitBreaker component that tracks per-region error rate, request queue depth, and recent fallback counts; it exposes states: CLOSED, PROBING, DEGRADED, OPEN. 2) routing: when a region enters DEGRADED state the router applies a priority-degradation policy that (a) pins traffic to cheaper local model variants, (b) enables permissive prefix-cache reads, (c) lowers batch targets for that region, and (d) funnels high-cost requests to a queued reserve pool. 3) control plane: add canary thresholds and an automatic decay window so regions exit DEGRADED after stability. 4) observability: new metrics (regional_cb_state, regional_cb_trips_total, regional_degradation_score), Grafana dashboard panels, and SLO-aware alerts. 5) ops: an emergency rollback flag and a graceful drain script. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-6421) - [x] unit tests for breaker state transitions - [x] integration tests with router simulator - [x] e2e smoke in staging (us-west only) - [x] dashboard and alert runbook updated - [x] staged rollout plan approved by SRE Implementation notes: commits: - feat(cb): add RegionalCircuitBreaker and state machine (Maya Chen) - feat(router): hook degradation policies and priority routing (Arjun Patel) - perf: adjust batching heuristics when region is DEGRADED (Liam O'Connor) - docs: add runbook and dashboard panels (Sofia Martinez) Files changed (high level): - runtime/circuit/regional_cb.go: new state machine, configuration knobs, unit tests - routing/priority_degradation.go: policy application, variant pinning logic - controlplane/decay_scheduler.py: decay windows, canary thresholds - observability/grafana/panels.json: dashboard panels and alerts - ops/drain-scripts/degraded-drain.sh: safe-drain script used by SRE - docs/runbooks/regional-cb.md: runbook and rollback steps Testing & validation: staged rollout on staging -> canary (us-west-2) -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> global. We ran synthetic failure injection against us-west to validate: breaker tripped into DEGRADED, request latency improved 22% relative to naive failover, and total cross-region egress decreased by 38%. CI: unit tests and integration tests passed locally and in CI after two retries (flake in simulator fixed). Backwards compatibility: config knobs default to conservative thresholds; feature disabled for tenants without opt-in. Rollback plan: set controlplane.toggle.regional_cb=false and trigger immediate drain script; documented in runbook. Related: SRE-881 (regional incident postmortem), SUP-1983 (customer-facing errors in us-west). Merge: approved by reviewers (see conversation), merged via squash on 2026-03-04.
